Article Title: After admitting 'hardest year' yet in its 13-year history, Canva announces major job cuts; CEO sends long 'layoff email'
Article Text:
CEO calls it Canva's toughest year

Canva layoffs : 22% of workforce affected

Support package for affected employees

Major organisational overhaul planned

Read Canva CEO Melanie Perkins’ email to employees here

Hi everyone,

Today, I have some profoundly difficult news to share.

After months of thinking through how to set Canva up for the next chapter, we have made the incredibly hard decision to make significant changes to how we’re organised, where some of our teams are based, and the roles and skills we need for the future.

This means 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, will be impacted. For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs. Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today.

This is without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history. Behind every decision is someone we care deeply about, and I know the consequences will be very real for those directly affected, their families, friends and teammates.

I’m deeply sorry for the pain and disruption this will cause for everyone affected. While nothing can make this news easier, we will do everything we possibly can to support everyone affected.

I want to explain as openly as I can why we're making these changes, how we reached these decisions, and, most importantly, how we will care for the people affected today.

Why we’re making these changes

We've spoken a lot about how quickly the world is changing. New technology is transforming what people can create, how they create it, and what they expect from the products they use.

Over the past thirteen years, we’ve turned a dream in a pitch deck into a platform used by hundreds of millions of people.

None of it would have been possible without the talent, imagination and care of every single person who has been part of this journey. Yet success in our first chapter doesn’t guarantee success in the next. This has been our hardest year yet, and as we shared earlier this year, our growth has slowed for the first time in a decade.

After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I've come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough.

To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership and focus on what matters most for our community.

It also means making some of the hardest decisions we've ever faced, including saying goodbye to people who have helped make Canva what it is today. For that, I am deeply sorry.

What we’re changing

We're making three changes to bring more of what has made Canva special back into how we work.

#1. We're simplifying how we come together to build Canva

As we've grown, more of our work has become organised around team structures and narrow areas of ownership. Improving one part of our product often requires navigating between Product, Growth and Platform, with more handovers and coordination than necessary. This has made it harder to take ownership of bigger problems and to build a deeply unified product for our community.

We’ve tried many ways to solve this over the years, but it’s become clear we need to revisit our underlying structure.

To do that, we’re bringing Product, Growth and Platform together into one Product Org and changing the way we work to provide clearer ownership, greater autonomy and flexibility to tackle our most important goals. We want to get back to spending more time building, and less time navigating how work gets done.

#2. We’re reducing subspecialisation and collapsing layers to broaden ownership

Over time, we've divided work across more and more subspecialties and teams. While this has helped us build valuable expertise, it's also fragmented ownership and made it harder to see the full picture, with different teams responsible for many pieces of the same work.

We're reducing this fragmentation and incorporating narrower subspecialties into broader roles so teams have more ownership of goals from start to finish.

We're also simplifying layers, consolidating overlapping responsibilities, and ensuring teams have the right mix of skills and experience for the chapter ahead.

#3. We’re co-locating closely connected teams and increasing in-person collaboration

Working across countries has brought enormous benefits and talent, but it’s also made it harder to bring the right people together to solve complex problems. We’ll continue investing in our global team, particularly where being close to our community, customers and markets matters most.

At the same time, Sydney will become the primary home for more of our product teams, as well as roles in other Specialties where shared context and close collaboration are especially important. We know relocating is a big decision for those being asked to consider it, and we're committed to making the process as smooth as possible with comprehensive support.

We also want to bring more teams together in person to build trust, learn from one another and strengthen the connections that make Canva special.

From January, we expect most Hybrid Canvanauts to spend around 2 to 3 days in the office each week, depending on what makes sense in your area.

How we approached these decisions

I know many of you will have questions about how we made these decisions. We began with one question: what does Canva need to do to succeed in the chapter ahead?

We started with our mission and future goals, then considered the structures, skills and locations needed to achieve them.

Only then did we look at what this would mean for individual roles. While understanding how we reached these decisions won't make them any less painful, I want to emphasise that they are not a reflection of the talent, care and dedication people have brought to Canva, their skills or the enormous contributions they've made along the way.

Supporting those who are leaving

We know everyone's circumstances are different, and while nothing can make today’s news easy, we've tried to reflect those different needs in the financial, career and wellbeing support we're providing to everyone affected:

Everyone will receive at least six months of salary, inclusive of statutory entitlements, regardless of location.

Removing the one-year vesting cliff for those who joined in the past year.

Twelve months of continued healthcare coverage in countries where we currently provide this.

Twelve months of Canva Care (our EAP), with this coverage also extending to family members.

Dedicated career support, including one-on-one coaching, interview preparation, and one year of LinkedIn Premium. We're also dedicating a significant portion of our Talent Acquisition team to helping people review their resumes and practice for interviews to find their next opportunity.

An opt-in alumni talent directory that we'll proactively share with our investors, partners, and wider industry network to help connect departing Canvanauts with new roles.

Everyone leaving will be able to keep their Canva MacBook as we know not everyone has a personal laptop.

We’re also launching the Canva Collective Fund, providing US$10,000 grants to departing Canvanauts who want to start something of their own.

Whether it’s starting a business or doing something meaningful for their local community, the fund is designed to help get those ideas off the ground. Everyone leaving as part of these changes will have until the 14 of December to register their interest, and we won’t take any ownership or equity in what they create.

What happens next

Our immediate priority is to make time for the conversations with everyone directly impacted by these changes.

Those impacted will receive a calendar invite for an individual meeting with a senior leader in their area to discuss the next steps and support available should they wish to attend.

With teams across 37 countries, we'll need to follow different local requirements and processes, which means the timing and way these conversations happen may vary depending on where people are based.

We also want to give everyone the time to process this news and say goodbye in their own way.

Everyone leaving Canva will continue to have access to Slack and Gmail until the end of the week, so they can choose when and how to share the news with their teams. This means you may not know exactly how your team is changing straight away, and we ask everyone to respect the privacy of those having these conversations. Leads will share more about the changes to different areas by the end of the week.

We've put together some answers to common questions and everything you need to know.

There's no need to read through everything right now, but we hope they'll be helpful whenever you're ready. Next week, we’ll come together for a Company All Hands on November 10th to talk through these changes, answer questions, and share more about the path ahead. We’ve asked Org Leads to wait until after this to bring their teams together, with Org All Hands taking place from November 11th.

To everyone continuing at Canva: I know this news will be incredibly difficult, especially as we say goodbye to friends and teammates who have been such an important part of our journey.

Please look after yourselves and one another and be there for those who are leaving. We’re also cancelling non-critical meetings for the rest of the week, and encourage anyone who needs some time and space to process this news to take the day off.

There’s no need to log this as leave.

To those who will be leaving Canva: I wish I could adequately express how grateful I am for everything you've contributed. The Canva that exists today is the result of your hard work, creativity, passion and care.

Hundreds of millions of people around the world have been empowered by what you've helped build, and I hope you know just how much of a difference you've made. I am deeply sorry this is how your chapter at Canva is ending.

Please know these decisions do not diminish your talent, the value of your contributions, or the difference you've made here. We will do everything we can to support you in what comes next, and I hope the work we do from here will be worthy of what you've helped build.

Mel

Canva, the Australian design software company has announced a major job cuts at the company. This restructuring effort of the company will affect 1,271 employees, or about 22% of its global workforce, with co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins describing the move as "the hardest moment" in the company's 13-year history. The graphic design platform revealed the changes in a lengthy message to employees that was later published on the company's newsroom website. The announcement comes as Canva grapples with slowing growth and seeks to reshape its organisation for what it calls its next chapter. Perkins apologised to those affected for the pain and disruption.In the note, Perkins said the company had reached a difficult conclusion after months of reviewing its future direction. She acknowledged that the restructuring would result in layoffs, role changes, and relocation requests for some employees. "This has been our hardest year yet," Perkins wrote, adding that Canva's growth had slowed for the first time in a decade. According to the CEO, the company explored several alternatives before determining that smaller adjustments would not be enough to prepare the business for long-term success.She said the company needed to "refound Canva" by returning to its roots of smaller, empowered teams with greater ownership and autonomy.Canva said 1,271 people, representing roughly 22% of its workforce, will be affected by the changes. While some employees will leave the company, others may be asked to relocate to centralised hubs or transition into new roles. Perkins noted that the restructuring would impact people across teams and geographies. The company currently operates across 37 countries, with employees spread across a global network of offices and remote locations.The company has outlined a support package for affected workers. Canva said departing employees will receive at least six months of salary, including statutory entitlements, regardless of location. Other benefits include up to 12 months of healthcare coverage where applicable, career coaching, interview preparation, LinkedIn Premium subscriptions and access to an alumni talent network. Employees leaving the company will also be allowed to keep their Canva-issued MacBooks. In addition, the company is launching a Canva Collective Fund that will provide grants of US$10,000 to eligible departing employees interested in starting businesses or community projects.As part of the restructuring, Canva will merge its Product, Growth and Platform divisions into a single Product Organisation. The company said the move is intended to reduce internal handovers, simplify decision-making and provide teams with clearer ownership over projects. Canva is also reducing specialisation across certain functions, collapsing management layers and consolidating overlapping responsibilities. The company believes broader roles will allow teams to take end-to-end responsibility for their work rather than operating within narrower areas of expertise.Another key change involves location strategy. Canva said Sydney will become the primary base for more of its product teams, and some employees will be asked to relocate. Beginning in January, most hybrid employees will also be expected to spend two to three days each week in the office
Article Summary: CEO Melanie Perkins has announced 22% of Canva's workforce will be affected by a major organisational overhaul. Some people will be asked to relocate to centralised hubs. The company is also simplifying the way it works to make it easier for people to take ownership of problems.

Article Title: Scientist builds a mini universe of 24,000 atoms to show time can be measured without a clock
Article Text:
Representative Image

Entropy, not a clock, keeps time in this mini universe

A scientist at the University of Birmingham has built a mini universe out of about 24,000 atoms to show that time can be measured without a clock. Giovanni Barontini's experiment tracks the order of events purely through changes in entropy, the measure of disorder in a system.The result matters because physics still has no settled answer on what time is. General relativity and quantum mechanics describe it differently, and this lab-made universe offers a controlled way to study that mismatch.The atoms are rubidium, chilled to almost absolute zero, which is around minus 273 degrees Celsius. At that temperature they stop behaving like separate particles and act more like a single cloud.The cloud sits in a trap it cannot escape. A specially configured laser splits the trap into two halves. One is the bright side, which was observed. The other is the dark side, which stays unobserved.Only the bright side served as the timekeeper. Its entropy kept changing, and the internal timer moved forward only when atoms crossed the laser barrier between the two halves. By watching the cloud expand and contract, and by tracking the exchange of atoms, it became possible to work out the order in which events happened.There was a catch. When no atoms crossed over, the internal clock stopped. An external clock kept running anyway, so the two disagreed on when events took place. Inside this system, time did not match the time outside it.The experiment could help link relativity and quantum physicsBoth theories underpin modern physics, yet they do not always agree on how time works. In certain quantum systems, for instance, time can be reversed. Showing that time can be read from entropy changes in an atomic system is a step toward bringing the two together.Barontini's model is only a starting point. It leaves out factors such as black holes, and several settings can be changed, including the shape of the trap, the density of the atoms and the height of the laser barrier.The cloud's repeated swings between the dark and bright sides could also help scientists simulate conditions just after the Big Bang. It might even help model the lead-up to the Big Crunch, the theoretical point at which the universe collapses into itself.The full impact will take a while to show. For now, it answers a simple question: you do not need a clock to tell time, as long as something keeps changing.
Article Summary: Giovanni Barontini's experiment tracks the order of events purely through changes in entropy, the measure of disorder in a system. The experiment could help link relativity and quantum physics. It could also help scientists simulate conditions just after the Big Bang.

Article Title: Hours after US mid-term election results, Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message to Google, Amazon, Meta and other companies building data centres; says: Right now …
Article Text:
Elon Musk sends 'let's go to Space' message hours after mid-term election results

Democrats wins Texas

US mid-term election rewrites history

Hours after mid-term election results, Elon Musk said that building data centres in space look increasingly “appealing right now”. The post comes following the Democrats’ strong performance in the US mid-term elections. Musk, who has been a prominent Republican supporter during the election cycle and reportedly spent over $150 million in Texas alone, shared two posts on X (formerly Twitter). “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk wrote in the early hours of Wednesday, November 4, after election results pointed to a major victory for Democrats.“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time 🤷‍♂️,” Musk said in the second post, appearing to joke about his political influence and the election outcome.The comments came as Democrats made significant gains, including a surprise victory in Texas’ governor’s race by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who has opposed data centre expansion. Notably, Elon Musk and his companies – Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI have a growing footprint of high-performance computing (HPC), chip manufacturing, and data center-related infrastructure projects across Texas.Musk’s posts did not directly address companies such as Google , Amazon and Meta, which are expanding their data centre infrastructure to support AI development.The billionaire's remark on data centres come as the AI industry faces growing political scrutiny over massive data centers, with concerns about electricity costs and environmental impacts becoming campaign issues.The 2026 midterm elections in the US had a series of historic firsts so far. Voters elected the country's first Black woman governor, first Native American woman governor, first Native American woman senator and first openly gay male senator in the mid-term elections.The elections also set a records for women's political participation. According to Rutgers University's Center for American Women and Politics, nearly 300 women ran for the US House and Senate.
Article Summary: Elon Musk says data centres in space look 'appealing right now' Comments come as Democrats make significant gains in US mid-term elections. Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI have a growing footprint of high-performance computing (HPC) and data center-related infrastructure projects across Texas.

Article Title: Sachin Tendulkar's record gone! Virat Kohli creates history during India's New Zealand chase
Article Text:
Virat Kohli celebrates after scoring 50 runs during the first ODI against New Zealand. (AP/PTI Photo)

Kohli equals Ponting's record against New Zealand

Most ODI runs against New Zealand

1971 - Virat Kohli

1971 - Ricky Ponting

1750 - Sachin Tendulkar

1568 - Kumar Sangakkara

1519 - Sanath Jayasuriya

1449 - Jacques Kallis

First batter to reach 13,000 ODI runs at No. 3

Most ODI runs at No. 3

Virat Kohli - 13,000*

Ricky Ponting - 12,662

Kumar Sangakkara - 9,747

Jacques Kallis - 7,774

Kane Williamson - 6,504

Kohli-Gill partnership puts India in control

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli continued to rewrite the record books on Wednesday, breaking Sachin Tendulkar 's long-standing record for the most runs in successful and unsuccessful ODI run chases during India's rain-affected first ODI against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland.The former India captain produced another masterclass in chasing, scoring a fluent 74 off just 51 deliveries as India overhauled a revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs in a contest reduced to 32 overs per side by rain. Kohli's innings, which featured 13 fours and a six, set the tone for India's chase after an early setback.With his knock, Kohli took his tally of runs in ODI chases to 8,741, moving past Tendulkar's previous record of 8,720. He now stands alone at the top of the all-time list, further strengthening his reputation as one of the greatest chase masters the game has witnessed.The numbers underline Kohli's remarkable consistency in this format. He has scored his 8,741 runs in chases at an average of 66.21 and a strike rate of 95.03. Tendulkar, meanwhile, finished with 8,720 runs at an average of 42.33 and a strike rate of 88.44.The 37-year-old added another significant milestone to his ODI career, equalling Ricky Ponting's record for the most runs against New Zealand in the format.Kohli now has 1,971 ODI runs against the Black Caps, drawing level with the former Australia captain, who accumulated the same number during his illustrious career. With more matches remaining in the ongoing series, Kohli has an opportunity to move past Ponting and claim the record outright.Former India great Tendulkar is third on the list with 1,750 runs against New Zealand, followed by Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara (1,568) and Sanath Jayasuriya (1,519).Kohli also became the first batter in ODI history to reach 13,000 runs while batting at the No. 3 position.He achieved the landmark during his innings against New Zealand, taking his tally at the position to exactly 13,000 at an extraordinary average of 61.61.Before Kohli, only Tendulkar had crossed the 13,000-run mark at a particular batting position in ODI cricket. The Master Blaster scored 13,685 runs while batting at No. 2.Kohli now leads the list of leading run-scorers at No. 3, comfortably ahead of Ponting, who finished with 12,662 runs, and Sangakkara, who accumulated 9,747.Kohli's milestones came during a commanding partnership with Shubman Gill , who helped India recover after Rohit Sharma departed in the opening over.The duo stitched together a crucial 113-run stand for the second wicket, taking control of a tricky chase that had already been interrupted by rain. While Gill took time to settle in, Kohli looked in sublime touch, finding gaps regularly and punishing loose deliveries through the off-side and square-leg regions.Kohli accelerated after the first rain interruption, but his entertaining knock eventually ended in the 20th over when he attempted to pull Jacob Duffy's short delivery. He failed to control the shot and was caught by Tim Seifert at deep backward square leg for 74.India did lose a few wickets in quick succession towards the end, but with fewer than 30 runs required, the result was never seriously in doubt.It was another vintage Kohli performance — a combination of composure, controlled aggression and remarkable consistency — as India began the New Zealand ODI series with a victory.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli equals Ricky Ponting's record for most runs against New Zealand. First batter to reach 13,000 ODI runs at No. 3 position. Sachin Tendulkar's record of most runs in successful and unsuccessful ODI run chases also broken.

Article Title: Hockey legend MM Somaya's house burgled in Bengaluru; 4 international medals stolen
Article Text:
While hockey great MM Somaya was away in Kodagu, his home in New Thippasandra fell victim to a burglary





BENGALURU: Miscreants broke into the house of hockey legend MM Somaya in New Thippasandra, Indiranagar, and fled with valuables, including the gold medal he won as part of the Indian hockey team at the 1980 Moscow Olympics.According to sources, the burglary took place while Somaya and his family were away in his hometown Kodagu between October 25 and October 28.According to the FIR registered at Indiranagar police station, Somaya left his residence at around 5pm on October 25 and returned at approximately 7.15am on October 28. He discovered that the house had been burgled.The stolen items included several medals from his career in international hockey: the gold medal from the 1980 Moscow Olympics, a silver medal from the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi, a bronze medal from the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul, and another bronze medal from the 1982 Champions Trophy held in Amsterdam.
Article Summary: Hockey legend MM Somaya's home in New Thippasandra, Indiranagar, burgled. Stolen items included gold medal from 1980 Moscow Olympics. Somaya and his family were away in his hometown Kodagu between October 25 and October 28.

Article Title: Bombay HC says Mumbai corporators playing no role in garbage removal
Article Text:
HC was hearing a petition by Kannamwar Nagar CHS regarding pollution from the Kanjurmarg dumping ground

Mumbai:





Bombay High Court on Tuesday asked how many corporators in Mumbai had worked to remove garbage and prevent pollution in their wards.“Those who are supposed to do this, they should be doing this. We don’t find any role of corporators,” said Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale.HC was hearing a petition by Kannamwar Nagar CHS regarding pollution from the Kanjurmarg dumping ground. On Oct 22, HC sought to know if the right of slum dwellers to re-accommodation can be forfeited if they do not cooperate in maintaining hygiene and in garbage disposal. Senior advocate Birendra Saraf, for SRA, said statutory provisions do not confer such a power upon SRA.The judges said BMC’s AI-operated cameras and mist sprinkler systems, if operationalised in slums, will make a difference. Senior advocate Anil Sakhare, for BMC, said at every point where there is garbage dumped, it will be installed. Saraf then said SRA can possibly also organise awareness camps.Justice Gokhale said, “Now, we can’t even ask famous people to come forward and run these campaigns.” Justice Kulkarni added, “You try to do something good for the public, a different colour is given. This is what we have experienced [in the firecrackers matter.Here also the court is concerned with the environment, cleanliness, hygiene etc.”Sakhare said corporators are requested to participate to raise community awareness. “Show us one corporator in Mumbai, maybe a new corporator or old corporator, who had terms and terms of corporation elections, that he has done something for his ward in respect of the slum areas and removal of garbage, cleanliness, and maintenance. Corporator in Kannamwar Nagar, how many times has he taken up the matter of pollution?” asked Justice Kulkarni. Justice Gokhale said HPC’s report shows the mayor had only distributed saplings and plants.The judges noted that despite BMC’s measures and the contractor’s installing 27 mist sprinklers, there was no improvement. Petitioner’s advocate Abhijeet Rane said residents are getting odour throughout the night. The judges will appoint three advocates as amici curiae (friends of the court) “to know what is lacking… so that things can be put in proper perspective.”
Article Summary: HC was hearing a petition by Kannamwar Nagar CHS regarding pollution from the Kanjurmarg dumping ground. Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale asked how many corporators in Mumbai had worked to remove garbage and prevent pollution in their wards.

Article Title: Kolhapur’s pothole nightmare set to continue as contractors refuse repairs
Article Text:
A pothole on the road between Panchganga ghat and Shivaji bridge

Kolhapur

:





Residents are unlikely to get any respite from commuting woes this Diwali. After enduring bumpy, pothole-ridden roads through Ganesh Chaturthi and Navaratra, commuters will still have to navigate damaged streets, as several contractors have refused to start repairs despite receiving official work orders.Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC) has approved 64 road repair projects worth Rs 62 crore for the 2026-27 financial year. Work on the ground, however, remains largely stalled, with contractors citing a steep rise in asphalt (tar) prices and claiming the projects were no longer financially viable.The deadlock has left the city’s roads scarred and commuters frustrated, turning what should have been a festive season into a test of patience for motorists and pedestrians alike.Social activist Amar Patil slammed the civic administration for the delay. “Roads that were supposed to be repaired before Ganesh Chaturthi are still riddled with potholes. Daily commuting has become a struggle. KMC must crack down on contractors who are refusing to execute the work despite receiving orders. At this rate, smooth roads in Kolhapur seem like an impossible dream,” he said.Responding to the criticism, KMC commissioner Rajendra Bharud acknowledged the standoff and urged contractors to either seek a collective solution from govt or begin work immediately. “Road projects covering 64 roads and costing Rs 62 crore have been approved. Contractors are, however, unwilling to undertake the work due to the increase in asphalt prices. They should jointly approach govt for a resolution or start the work without further delay,” Bharud said.With the prevailing situation, the residents may once again find themselves celebrating the festival amid traffic snarls, dust and potholes, waiting for roads that have been promised but are nowhere in sight.
Article Summary: Kolhapur Municipal Corporation has approved 64 road repair projects worth Rs 62 crore for the 2026-27 financial year. Work on the ground, however, remains largely stalled, with contractors citing a steep rise in asphalt (tar) prices and claiming the projects were no longer financially viable.

Article Title: First on-camera tiger sighting by tourists recorded at Radhanagari-Dajipur sanctuary
Article Text:
Male Tiger STR-T10 at Dajipur Wildlife Sanctuary

Kolhapur





: Tourists visiting Radhanagari-Dajipur Wildlife Sanctuary had a rare wildlife encounter on Monday morning when they caught a glimpse of a male Bengal tiger.The big cat, identified as STR-T10 ‘Ranoji’, was spotted during a jungle safari in the sanctuary’s core zone. Forest department officials said this is the first time a tiger has been officially sighted and recorded on camera by tourists in Dajipur sanctuary, with both photographs and video footage verifying the event.The thrilling encounter took place just a day after the forest department officially resumed wildlife safaris for the new tourism season on Nov 1.Safari vehicle driver Prasad Korgaonkar, who was guiding three tourists from Rukadi, described the moment. “This was my very first ride since safaris resumed. During the trek, we first came across a jungle hen, a snake, and a gaur, before suddenly spotting Ranoji resting under a canopy of trees. While we regularly see gaurs in this region, witnessing a wild tiger was an unforgettable, thrilling experience.”Wildlife experts said the landmark sighting reinforces the ecological importance of the 341 sq km sanctuary, which serves as a vital corridor within the larger Sahyadri Tiger Reserve.Forest authorities attributed the successful sighting to strict conservation measures aimed at reducing human disturbance. The wildlife department has capped the number of active safari vehicles and restricted tour timings to a specific window between 6am and 2pm. Additionally, forest officials have dug 20 artificial water bodies throughout the sanctuary to ensure adequate drinking supply for the wildlife. To maintain strict safety standards and operational order, every safari vehicle is mandated to carry a registered guide.
Article Summary: Tourists visiting Radhanagari-Dajipur Wildlife Sanctuary had a rare wildlife encounter on Monday morning when they caught a glimpse of a male Bengal tiger. The big cat, identified as STR-T10 ‘Ranoji’, was spotted during a jungle safari in the sanctuary’s core zone. Forest department officials said this is the first time a tiger has been officially sighted and recorded on camera.
